text.p: The consulting firms Registry Inc and Renaissance Solutions Inc said Tuesday they will merge in a stock swap valued at about $430 million.
Under terms of the deal, which was approved by the boards of both companies, Renaissance shareholders will get 0.80 share of Registry for each of their Renaissance shares.
Yesterday Renaissance shares closed at 34-3/4, while Registry shares closed at 56-1/2.
The companies said the transaction would be accretive to earnings, excluding charges.
The new, combined company will take a charge of $9.0-$11.0 million in the September quarter for the deal, said Robert Foley, chief financial officer of Registry.
Foley will become CFO of the new company. Drew Conway, president and chief executive officer of Registry, will become the new company's president and CEO.
Based in Newton, Mass., Registry provides information technology consulting services. Renaissance, based in Lincoln, Mass., develops technology-based business solutions.
"There are a lot of synergies between the two companies...and a lot of opportunities within those synergies," said Foley.
He said there will "absolutely be no job losses" from the merger.
"We are likely to add jobs as we expand," he said.
The companies said the deal would close within the next 90 days, pending regulatory and shareholder approval.
